profile.campus: Clarksville-Montgomery County, Tennessee (Google's Boolean Drive / Jim Johnson Road campus)
profile.address: Boolean Drive, Montgomery County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee
profile.reading: This building, tagged SPC2A in OpenStreetMap, is part of the expansion of Google's Clarksville-Montgomery County data center campus beyond the original SPC1A building that opened in November 2019. Google, the Tennessee Valley Authority, and Governor Bill Haslam's administration announced the original roughly $600 million Clarksville project through the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development, with construction beginning in February 2018 and the first building opening in a ribbon-cutting ceremony led by then-Governor Bill Lee on November 6, 2019; subsequent buildings including this one followed as Google continued expanding the campus. The campus draws power in part through a 413-megawatt renewable energy purchase agreement Google struck with the Tennessee Valley Authority, sourced from solar farms totaling roughly 1.6 million panels across sites in Tennessee and Alabama. Google has said it gave more than $450,000 to local nonprofits and schools in the Clarksville area in the years following the data center's opening. Since construction began in 2018, Google reports investing more than $6 billion in Tennessee overall, a figure that under its updated economic-impact methodology includes data center construction along with server and networking capital expenditure rather than construction costs alone, and the company says it helped generate $11.4 billion of economic activity for Tennessee businesses, nonprofits, and developers in 2025. Google's data center locations page and its economic-impact reporting do not break these totals out per building, so this registry records them as regional context rather than facts specific to the SPC2A building, and treats the Boolean Drive address, drawn from OpenStreetMap's reverse-geocoded coordinates, as the best currently available location detail for this structure pending a county assessor parcel lookup.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center facility on Boolean Drive in the Clarksville-Montgomery County campus in Tennessee, part of a $600 million regional investment, but publishes no individual building capacity, square footage, or power specifications. Without disclosed watts, the facility's scale in terms of AI training racks cannot be calculated from published data.

Among the 24 mapped data center facilities in Tennessee, only 4 operators publish power capacity. Google's state total of published capacity ranks fifth and accounts for an unknown portion of those 12.13 megawatts, since the company discloses investment figures at the state level only, not at individual building level. Whether this Montgomery County building represents a major or minor share of Google's Tennessee footprint remains unpublished.

The campus cannot be assessed as a constraint on AI scaling without disclosure of its power consumption and IT load capacity. Prospective tenants and grid planners have only the $600 million investment figure and the operator's decision to omit site-specific specifications from public record.
